The derive-from-`safe-deployments` refactor is on point — the hash-equivalence argument for candidate ordering (`getSafeMigrationTargetVersions()` sort asc within `>=1.3.0`) is sound because all `>=1.3.0` domains and types are identical, so which candidate the loop picks does not change the resulting `safeTxHash`. A few things to consider:

### Suggestions

**1. Hardcoded singleton lists in `recipient-analysis.service.ts` are still there** — `src/modules/safe-shield/recipient-analysis/recipient-analysis.service.ts:65-72` (`SAFE_VERSIONS`) and `:82-86` (`MULTICHAIN_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`).

The PR body says "future SafeMigration/singleton releases are now covered by a safe-deployments dependency bump, with no code change." That is true for `SafeMigration` and `SafeToL2Migration`, but `SAFE_VERSIONS` is consumed by `determineMasterCopyVersion` (`:596-613`) — a v1.6.0 mastercopy will not be recognized here without editing this list. Same holds for `MULTICHAIN_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` used in `isNetworkCompatible` (`:642-646`). Consider deriving these from `getSafeSingletonVersions()` / `getSafeL2SingletonVersions()` in the same PR, or note it as a follow-up so the next release does not re-open a similar gap. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20src%2Fmodules%2Fsafe-shield%2Frecipient-analysis%2Frecipient-analysis.service.ts%20on%20branch%20tongyao%2Fwa-2933-cgw-recognise-the-150-migration-as-an-official-mastercopy%2C%20replace%20the%20hardcoded%20SAFE_VERSIONS%20(lines%2065-72)%20and%20MULTICHAIN_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS%20(lines%2082-86)%20with%20values%20derived%20from%20getSafeSingletonVersions%20and%20getSafeL2SingletonVersions%20so%20future%20singleton%20releases%20are%20recognised%20by%20determineMasterCopyVersion%20and%20isNetworkCompatible%20without%20a%20code%20change.&repo=safe-global/safe-client-gateway)

**2. Test still uses an inline literal version list** — `src/domain/common/utils/__tests__/safe.spec.ts:913`

```ts
const hasAnySingletons = ['1.3.0', '1.4.1', '1.5.0'].some((version) => { ... });
```

This defeats the purpose of deriving in production and will silently miss a future version. Use `getSafeSingletonVersions()` / `getSafeL2SingletonVersions()` (or the same `>=1.3.0` filter as production) so the guard tracks the package. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20src%2Fdomain%2Fcommon%2Futils%2F__tests__%2Fsafe.spec.ts%20line%20913%20on%20branch%20tongyao%2Fwa-2933-cgw-recognise-the-150-migration-as-an-official-mastercopy%2C%20replace%20the%20hardcoded%20%5B%271.3.0%27%2C%20%271.4.1%27%2C%20%271.5.0%27%5D%20list%20with%20a%20union%20of%20getSafeSingletonVersions%20and%20getSafeL2SingletonVersions%20filtered%20to%20%3E%3D1.3.0%20so%20the%20test%20tracks%20the%20safe-deployments%20package%20instead%20of%20drifting%20on%20new%20versions.&repo=safe-global/safe-client-gateway)

**3. Silent catch in `detectSafeMigration`** — `src/domain/common/utils/safe.ts:225`

Not new to this PR (pre-existing outer `try { ... } catch { return null; }`), but since the function is now the sole path for a real-world 422 failure mode, a debug/warn log on the caught error would help future incident triage instead of silently returning `null`.

**4. Minor: version-getter naming vs. semantics** — `getSafeSingletonVersions()` returns *all* versions the package ships (including pre-1.3.0 like `1.0.0`, `1.1.1`, `1.2.0`). That is fine for the current consumer because `getSafeMigrationTargetVersions()` filters by range, but any future caller that assumes "these are singleton versions I can safely feed into a SafeTx hash flow" could be tripped by the older entries. A short JSDoc note (or a helper that already filters `>=1.3.0`) would make the contract explicit.

### Nothing blocking

Changes look well-scoped and behaviorally correct. Tests exercise both `1.4.1` and `1.5.0` `SafeMigration` deployments and verify hash equivalence against an explicit `1.3.0` version — that is the right invariant to lock in.
